exam.title: Linux Foundation Certified IT Associate
exam.study_prerequisites: No formal prerequisites. Build beginner hands-on evidence across Linux and the command line; users, software, services, storage, networking, troubleshooting and recovery; cloud models, performance, availability and cost; identity, systems, networks, sensitive data and compliance; DevOps, Git and containers; plus project management, application architecture, functional analysis and open-source licensing.

review.notes: All six September 2025 weighted domains are connected through three beginner scenarios, eight safe labs and 40 original checks. The retired LFCA-JP and pre-update Supporting Applications/Developers wording are explicit. All seven guide URLs are cataloged and reachable in the dated run. No proprietary questions or course content are used.

findings.title: Staging is a snapshot rather than a live file link
findings.evidence: The Git manual says add records content at the time of the command; later changes require another add.
findings.recommendation: Add and execute a three-snapshot exercise, cached/ordinary diffs and unstaging that preserves later working content.
findings.resolution: Add and execute a three-snapshot exercise, cached/ordinary diffs and unstaging that preserves later working content.

findings.title: An ignore rule does not remove tracking or history
findings.evidence: Git documents that tracked files are not affected by ignore patterns; removing a path from the index is distinct from deleting history.
findings.recommendation: Explain and locally test tracked/untracked synthetic logs, retained working bytes and prior commit content; no real secret used.
findings.resolution: Explain and locally test tracked/untracked synthetic logs, retained working bytes and prior commit content; no real secret used.

findings.title: Conflict abort requires a suitable starting state
findings.evidence: Git warns that pre-existing uncommitted changes may not be fully reconstructible after an interrupted merge.
findings.recommendation: Use a clean synthetic repository, verify abort restores the main branch content, then resolve a second conflict against an explicit accepted requirement.
findings.resolution: Use a clean synthetic repository, verify abort restores the main branch content, then resolve a second conflict against an explicit accepted requirement.

findings.title: Package trust wording collapsed different signature mechanisms
findings.evidence: APT authenticates repository Release metadata and the package-checksum chain; it does not audit package code or verify each package-level signature.
findings.recommendation: Correct the package-management teaching and retain repository trust and behavior verification as separate evidence.
findings.resolution: Correct the package-management teaching and retain repository trust and behavior verification as separate evidence.

findings.title: Enabled, running and available are separate observations
findings.evidence: The manual says enable does not imply start and disable does not imply stop, with --now available for runtime actions.
findings.recommendation: Add state/activation/readiness distinctions, socket/static/dependency qualifications and proposed Linux evidence checks.
findings.resolution: Add state/activation/readiness distinctions, socket/static/dependency qualifications and proposed Linux evidence checks.

findings.title: File write permission alone does not decide deletion
findings.evidence: Linux unlink documents parent write/search, traversal and sticky-directory restrictions.
findings.recommendation: Teach operation-specific directory versus file permission reasoning without claiming MSYS proves Linux access-control behavior.
findings.resolution: Teach operation-specific directory versus file permission reasoning without claiming MSYS proves Linux access-control behavior.

findings.title: The shared-kernel statement needs a host-runtime boundary
findings.evidence: Docker describes isolated processes sharing a kernel and containers running within VMs.
findings.recommendation: Clarify Linux containers on a non-Linux workstation may share the runtime VM kernel; no container was executed.
findings.resolution: Clarify Linux containers on a non-Linux workstation may share the runtime VM kernel; no container was executed.

findings.title: Readable source alone does not establish open-source rights
findings.evidence: The OSD imposes redistribution, modification and use conditions beyond access to source.
findings.recommendation: Clarify license grant, obligations and component inventory; SPDX identification is not a compatibility opinion.
findings.resolution: Clarify license grant, obligations and component inventory; SPDX identification is not a compatibility opinion.

local_validation.execution_boundary: Native Git for Windows and MSYS Bash only; disposable synthetic repositories/files, no remotes, network, credential, hooks, global Git configuration, Linux VM, account/service/package/firewall/container/cloud actions. Complete Linux labs remain proposed.

limitations: Same-context AI review; independent human review pending.
35 local checks passed with Git 2.55.0.windows.5, MSYS Bash 5.3.15 and Python 3.13.14; all owned disposable repositories/files cleaned.

No remote, credentials, external messages, network service, global Git configuration, Linux VM, account, package, service, firewall, container or cloud mutation in the examples. Full eight labs remain proposed.
Native Linux runtime remains blocked from the earlier WSL startup attempt and is deferred for tomorrow; MSYS does not validate native Linux permissions, systemd, package or networking behavior.
The exact public Git script checks a synthetic file requirement; it does not demonstrate a running application, server protection rules, remote CI or production merge policy.
Project critical path, cloud costs/capacity, request errors and recovery timestamps are invented arithmetic cases, not measured service behavior or current prices.
GNU-hosted Bash manual timed out; targeted sections were read from the maintainer-hosted GNU Bash reference and checked against installed runtime behavior. The timeout is retained in fetch evidence.
Paid catalog metadata only; LFS200/Pluralsight public outlines retain older final-domain wording, and Coursera timing displays conflict. No paid lessons, questions or labs accessed.
